concepts.label: Vaginal bleeding
concepts.definition: Any bleeding or spotting per vagina during the current pregnancy.

concepts.label: Convulsions / fits
concepts.definition: Fits, seizures or convulsions.

concepts.label: Severe headache
concepts.definition: Headache described as severe, very bad, persistent, or not relieved by usual measures. A headache without any severity qualifier is `headache`.

concepts.label: Blurred vision / visual disturbance
concepts.definition: Blurred or dim vision, seeing spots or flashing lights, sudden loss of vision.

concepts.label: Fever
concepts.definition: Reported fever or feeling hot. A measured temperature goes in vitals.

concepts.label: Severe abdominal pain
concepts.definition: Abdominal (including epigastric) pain described as severe or very bad. Abdominal pain without a severity qualifier is `abdominal_pain`.

concepts.label: Reduced or absent fetal movement
concepts.definition: The baby is moving less than usual or has stopped moving.

concepts.label: Difficulty breathing
concepts.definition: Shortness of breath, fast or difficult breathing.

concepts.label: Swelling of face or hands
concepts.definition: Swelling (oedema) of the face or hands, or generalised swelling. Swelling limited to the feet or ankles is `leg_oedema`.

concepts.label: Leaking or gush of fluid (waters breaking)
concepts.definition: Fluid draining or gushing from the vagina before labour.

concepts.label: Severe vomiting
concepts.definition: Vomiting described as severe, persistent, or unable to keep food or fluids down. Ordinary morning sickness is `nausea_vomiting`.

concepts.label: Unconscious / unresponsive
concepts.definition: Loss of consciousness, fainting with unresponsiveness, cannot be woken.

concepts.label: Severe pallor
concepts.definition: Very pale palms, conjunctivae or tongue noted on examination or reported.

concepts.label: Looks very ill
concepts.definition: The health worker states the woman looks very ill or is in a bad state.

concepts.label: Headache (not described as severe)
concepts.definition: Headache without a severity qualifier.

concepts.label: Abdominal pain (not described as severe)
concepts.definition: Abdominal or lower abdominal pain without a severity qualifier.

concepts.label: Nausea and vomiting
concepts.definition: Nausea or vomiting not described as severe.

concepts.label: Heartburn
concepts.definition: Burning feeling in the chest or upper abdomen, indigestion.

concepts.label: Leg cramps
concepts.definition: Painful cramps in the legs.

concepts.label: Constipation
concepts.definition: Hard or infrequent stools.

concepts.label: Low back pain
concepts.definition: Pain in the lower back.

concepts.label: Pelvic pain
concepts.definition: Pain in the pelvis or pubic area.

concepts.label: Varicose veins
concepts.definition: Swollen, visible veins, usually in the legs.

concepts.label: Swelling of feet or ankles
concepts.definition: Swelling limited to the feet, ankles or legs.

concepts.label: Dizziness
concepts.definition: Feeling dizzy or light-headed, without loss of consciousness.

concepts.label: Tiredness / weakness
concepts.definition: Feeling tired, weak or lacking energy.

concepts.label: Cough
concepts.definition: Cough of any duration.

concepts.label: Abnormal vaginal discharge
concepts.definition: Vaginal discharge that is itchy, smelly, coloured or otherwise abnormal.

concepts.label: Painful or burning urination
concepts.definition: Pain or burning when passing urine.

rules.name: Vaginal bleeding
rules.message: Vaginal bleeding in pregnancy: refer now.

rules.name: Convulsions
rules.message: Convulsions in pregnancy (possible eclampsia): refer now.

rules.name: Severe headache
rules.message: Severe headache: check BP and refer now.

rules.name: Blurred vision
rules.when: Blurred vision / visual disturbance (present or possible)
rules.message: Blurred vision in pregnancy: check BP and refer now.

rules.name: Fever
rules.message: Fever in pregnancy: test for malaria and refer.

rules.name: Severe abdominal pain
rules.message: Severe abdominal pain in pregnancy: refer now.

rules.name: Reduced fetal movement
rules.when: Reduced or absent fetal movement (present or possible)
rules.message: Baby moving less or not at all: refer now.

rules.name: Difficulty breathing
rules.message: Difficulty breathing in pregnancy: refer now.

rules.name: Swelling of face or hands
rules.when: Swelling of face or hands (present or possible)
rules.message: Swelling of face or hands: check BP and urine protein, then refer.

rules.name: Leaking fluid before labour
rules.when: Leaking or gush of fluid (waters breaking) (present or possible)
rules.message: Waters breaking or leaking fluid: refer now.

rules.name: Severe vomiting
rules.message: Severe vomiting: check for dehydration and refer.

rules.name: Unconscious
rules.message: Unconscious or unresponsive: emergency referral now.

rules.name: Severe pallor
rules.message: Severe pallor (possible severe anaemia): check Hb/PCV and refer.

rules.name: Severe hypertension
rules.message: BP at or above 160/110: severe hypertension, refer now.

rules.name: Hypertension
rules.message: BP at or above 140/90: check urine protein and refer for assessment.

rules.name: Possible pre-eclampsia
rules.when: ((systolic BP ≥ 140 or diastolic BP ≥ 90) AND (Severe headache (present or possible) or Blurred vision / visual disturbance (present or possible) or Severe abdominal pain (present or possible) or Swelling of face or hands (present or possible) or urine protein is 2+ or 3+ or 4+))
rules.message: Raised BP with a pre-eclampsia sign: refer now.

rules.name: Severe anaemia
rules.message: Hb below 7 g/dL (or PCV below 21%): severe anaemia, refer now.

phrases.label: Leaking or gush of fluid (waters breaking)

questions: Is the danger-sign list in the vocabulary complete for Nigerian PHC practice? Add, merge or drop any?
Should "headache" with BP ≥ 140/90 be treated as a danger sign even when it is not described as severe?
Is "BP 14/9" shorthand common enough to rely on, or should it go to review?
Should a single BP number ("systolic 150") be recorded?
Is PCV < 21% an acceptable stand-in for Hb < 7 g/dL in the severe-anaemia rule?
Which edition and sections of the National Standing Orders should each rule cite?
Are there common local terms (English or Yoruba) for these signs that we are missing?
